n2-set-14-q-1.translation: Taking responsibility, I will resign as a council member.
n2-set-14-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: yameru / 辞める - to resign, step down, or quit an official post.

choices.reason: あきらめる means to give up or abandon hope; not the reading or meaning of 辞める.
うめる means to bury or fill in; not the reading of 辞める.
つとめる means to serve, work, or make an effort (務める/勤める/努める), not resign.
やめる is the correct reading of 辞める, meaning to step down or resign from an office.

n2-set-14-q-2.translation: LED bulbs have low power consumption and a long lifespan.
n2-set-14-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: shouhi / 消費 - consumption; 消費電力 means power consumption.

choices.reason: じょうひ incorrectly voices 消 as jyou.
しょうひ is the correct on-yomi reading of 消費 (shouhi).
しょうび incorrectly voices 費 as bi.
じょうび incorrectly voices both kanji as jyoubi.

n2-set-14-q-3.translation: It is important to make efforts toward the future with clear goals.
n2-set-14-q-3.correctAnswerEnglish: meikaku / 明確 - clear, distinct, definite.

choices.reason: めいたく misreads 確 as taku.
めいかく is the correct on-yomi reading of 明確 (clear/definite).
みょうたく uses the kan-on reading myou and misreads 確 as taku.
みょうかく uses myou instead of the standard mei for 明 in this word.

n2-set-14-q-4.translation: Because the cold weather suddenly returned, I caught a cold.
n2-set-14-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: gyakumodori / 逆戻り - reverting, returning back, or relapsing.

choices.reason: さかもどり uses the kun-yomi saka instead of the on-yomi gyaku.
ぎゃくもどり is the correct reading of 逆戻り (reversion/turning back).
ぎゃくもとり fails to voice 戻り (modori) in this compound.
さかさもどり is an incorrect reading using sakasa.

n2-set-14-q-5.translation: He is good at his job, but he has no sense of time.
n2-set-14-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: kannen / 観念 - sense, concept, awareness (時間の観念 = sense of time / punctuality).

choices.reason: がいねん is the reading of 概念 (general concept), not 観念.
けねん is the reading of 懸念 (concern/worry).
かんねん is the correct reading of 観念; 時間の観念 means a sense of time or punctuality.
りねん is the reading of 理念 (philosophy/ideology).

n2-set-14-q-6.translation: I make a conscious effort to have leeway both mentally and in terms of time.
n2-set-14-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: yoyuu / 余裕 - surplus, margin, leeway, or room to spare.

choices.reason: 予裕 uses 予 (beforehand) instead of 余 (surplus/remainder).
余裕 is the correct kanji combination for yoyuu (leeway/room to spare).
予有 uses 予 and 有, which is incorrect.
余有 uses 有 instead of 裕 (abundant).

n2-set-14-q-7.translation: My mobile phone broke, so I cannot get in touch with my friends.
n2-set-14-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: kowarete / 壊れて - broken or malfunctioning.

choices.reason: 壊れて is the correct kanji for kowarete, describing a broken device or machine.
傷れて is not a standard verb form; 傷つく means to get hurt or damaged.
破れて is yaburete (torn, ripped, or defeated).
崩れて is kuzurete (collapsed, crumbled).

n2-set-14-q-8.translation: I pay utility bills such as electricity and water by credit card.
n2-set-14-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: koukyou / 公共 - public or communal; 公共料金 means utility bills.

choices.reason: 公協 is not the word for public; 協 means cooperate.
交協 uses 交 (intersect/traffic) and 協, which is incorrect.
公共 is the correct kanji combination for koukyou (public/communal).
交共 uses 交 instead of 公.

n2-set-14-q-9.translation: Through education with stricter school rules and exams, juvenile delinquency was reduced.
n2-set-14-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: hanzai / 犯罪 - crime or offense; 少年犯罪 means juvenile delinquency.

choices.reason: 犯罰 combines crime and punishment (罰) and is read hanbatsu, not hanzai.
犯罪 is the correct kanji combination for hanzai (crime/offense).
反罰 uses 反 (anti/oppose) and 罰, which is incorrect.
反罪 uses 反 instead of 犯 (commit/perpetrate).

n2-set-14-q-10.translation: There are quite a few single women living alone who suffer burglaries.
n2-set-14-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: au / 遭う - to encounter or suffer (an undesirable event, damage, or crime).

choices.reason: 遂う is an invalid reading/kanji here; 遂げる means to accomplish.
遣う is tsukau (to use, dispatch).
逸う is not used for au; 逸らす/逸れる means to deviate or divert.
遭う is the correct kanji for suffering misfortune or crime (被害に遭う).

n2-set-14-q-11.translation: Regarding the procedures, please refer to the distributed booklet.
n2-set-14-q-11.correctAnswerEnglish: shousasshi / 小冊子 - booklet, pamphlet, or brochure.

choices.reason: 薄冊子 is not an established compound; the adjective form is 薄い冊子.
厚冊子 is not a compound.
大冊子 is not a standard Japanese term for a booklet.
小冊子 (shousasshi) is the standard compound meaning a booklet or brochure.

n2-set-14-q-12.translation: They say it takes 10 years to become a full-fledged artisan in this field.
n2-set-14-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: ichininmae / 一人前 - full-fledged, independent, adult, or fully qualified.

choices.reason: 一人力 (ichininriki) means the strength or labor of one person.
一人前 (ichininmae) is the established idiom meaning a fully qualified, independent professional.
一人者 (ichininsha) means the foremost authority or leader in a field, not a full-fledged worker.
一人並 is not standard; 人並み (hitonami) means average or ordinary.

n2-set-14-q-13.translation: The weekly magazine sensationalized the entertainer's private life.
n2-set-14-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: shiseikatsu / 私生活 - private life or personal life.

choices.reason: 俗生活 is not standard; 俗世 refers to the secular or mundane world.
個生活 is not an established compound; 個人 (individual) is used differently.
私生活 (shiseikatsu) is the standard term for a person's private life.
自生活 is not a valid Japanese compound.

n2-set-14-q-14.translation: In this area, wild animals sometimes wander into humans' sphere of living.
n2-set-14-q-14.correctAnswerEnglish: seikatsuken / 生活圏 - sphere of daily life / living territory.

choices.reason: 生活圏 (seikatsuken) is the established term meaning sphere or zone of daily life.
生活層 is not a natural compound; 層 typically designates social strata.
生活間 does not form a valid compound for living territory.
生活中 means 'in the middle of living' and cannot describe entering a territory.

n2-set-14-q-15.translation: Numbered tickets will be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
n2-set-14-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: senchakujun / 先着順 - first-come, first-served order.

choices.reason: 先着着 is redundant and not a valid word.
先着番 is not standard; the suffix for order of arrival is 順.
先着順 (senchakujun) is the standard expression meaning in order of arrival.
先着人 is not a word.

n2-set-14-q-16.translation: Around the time I took office as president in place of my father, all I thought about was wanting to surpass him.
n2-set-14-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: shuunin / 就任 - taking office, assuming an official post.

choices.reason: 社長に就任する is the correct collocation for assuming the post of company president.
交代 means replacement or alternation; one does not say 社長に交代した in this role-taking sense.
就職 means finding employment or getting a job, not assuming a presidency.
後任 is a noun meaning successor; it does not take する directly in this sentence structure.

n2-set-14-q-17.translation: That many elementary school pupils go to school without eating breakfast is a serious problem.
n2-set-14-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: shinkoku / 深刻 - serious, grave, acute (深刻な問題 = serious problem).

choices.reason: 皮肉 means ironic or sarcastic, not a grave social issue.
深刻 (shinkoku) means serious or grave; 深刻な問題 is the standard collocation.
格別 means exceptional or special, not serious.
真剣 means earnest or serious in attitude, but does not modify 問題 like 深刻 does.

n2-set-14-q-18.translation: My part-time jobs during my student days were purely for covering living expenses.
n2-set-14-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: junsui ni / 純粋に - purely, solely, entirely.

choices.reason: 平等に means equally or fairly, not purely for living expenses.
陽気に means cheerfully or merrily.
面倒に means troublesomely.
純粋に (junsui ni) means purely or solely, emphasizing that the sole purpose was living costs.

n2-set-14-q-19.translation: The route where the president was to pass was strictly guarded by a large number of police officers.
n2-set-14-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: genjuu / 厳重 - strict, tight, heavy (厳重に警備する = strictly guard).

choices.reason: 厳重に警備する is the standard collocation for tightly guarding or securing an area.
強力 means powerful or strong, not strict security.
膨大 means enormous or vast in quantity, not strict.
過多 means excessive or surplus, not strict.

n2-set-14-q-20.translation: In the horse racing world, winning the Derby is the highest source of pride.
n2-set-14-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: hokori / 誇り - pride, honor, boast (最高の誇り = greatest pride).

choices.reason: 栄え (sakae) means prosperity or glory, but 最高の誇り (greatest pride/honor) is the natural idiom.
譲り means conceding or inheriting.
誇り (hokori) means pride; 最高の誇り denotes the greatest source of pride or honor.
見ばえ means outward appearance or showiness.

n2-set-14-q-21.translation: Since it has gotten late, it is about time I took my leave. Thank you very much for the meal.
n2-set-14-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: sorosoro / そろそろ - about time, soon, gradually.

choices.reason: とうとう means at last or in the end after a prolonged process.
いよいよ means finally, at long last, or more and more.
そろそろ失礼致します is the standard polite formula for taking one's leave ('it is about time I went').
たまたま means by chance or accidentally.

n2-set-14-q-22.translation: As remarks continued regarding the amendment of the ordinance, the debate heated up.
n2-set-14-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: hiito appu / ヒートアップ - heat up, become heated or intense.

choices.reason: ヒートアップ accurately describes a debate or argument becoming heated and intense.
イメージアップ means improving one's public image.
バックアップ means backing up data or providing support.
タイアップ means a business collaboration or tie-up.

n2-set-14-q-23.translation: He denied / retracted his own statement.
n2-set-14-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: hitei shita / 否定した - denied or negated, matching 打ち消した.

choices.reason: 修正した means modified or corrected.
伝達した means transmitted or conveyed.
記録した means recorded.
否定した means denied, directly paraphrasing 打ち消した (negated/denied).

n2-set-14-q-24.translation: This newspaper article criticizing politics is very sharp / incisive.
n2-set-14-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: sugurete iru / 優れている - excellent, outstanding, perceptive; matches 鋭い in this context.

choices.reason: 間違っている means incorrect or mistaken.
優れている means excellent or perceptive, capturing the keen insight of 鋭い (sharp/incisive).
冷静である means calm or composed.
読まれている means widely read.

n2-set-14-q-25.translation: Ms. Kimura is constantly checking her mobile phone emails.
n2-set-14-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: itsumo / いつも - always or constantly, matching 始終 (shijuu).

choices.reason: 何度か means several times.
いつも means always or all the time, directly matching 始終 (continuously from start to finish).
はじめに means at the beginning or first.
たまに means occasionally or once in a while.

n2-set-14-q-26.translation: I am entrusting this work to you, so do your best as much as you can.
n2-set-14-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: dekiru dake / できるだけ - as much as possible, matching せいぜい (to the utmost).

choices.reason: いいかげんに means half-heartedly or carelessly.
つらくても means even if it is painful or hard.
できるだけ means as much as possible, matching せいぜい used in an encouraging imperative sense.
最後まで means until the very end.

n2-set-14-q-27.translation: If we implement this plan, what advantages will there be?
n2-set-14-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: yuuri na ten / 有利な点 - advantageous points / benefits, matching メリット.

choices.reason: 不利な点 means disadvantageous points (demerits).
有利な点 means advantageous points, directly matching メリット (merits/advantages).
疑問点 means doubtful or questionable points.
問題点 means problematic points or issues.

n2-set-14-q-28.translation: Japan relies on imports for the vast majority of its energy.
n2-set-14-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: taihan / 大半 - the majority, most, or greater part of.

choices.reason: For reaching an amount like 2 trillion yen, 約 (approximately) or およそ fits; 大半 cannot modify a numerical total like this.
エネルギーの大半を輸入に頼っている correctly uses 大半 to mean the vast majority of a whole.
For evidence being plentiful, 十分 (sufficiently) or 数多く fits; 大半 cannot adverbially modify having evidence.
For amassing wealth, 莫大な富 (enormous wealth) or 多額の fits; 大半 cannot modify 富 as an adjective here.

n2-set-14-q-29.translation: My husband uses work socializing as a pretext to come home drinking every night.

choices.reason: 仕事の付き合いを口実に correctly uses 口実 meaning a pretext or excuse to justify an action.
Picking up a wallet was the trigger or opportunity (きっかけ), not a pretext (口実).
For borrowing money, there are conditions or rules (条件/手続き), not 口実.
Bullying would be the actual cause or reason (原因/理由), not an excuse or pretext (口実).

n2-set-14-q-30.translation: The public was disappointed in the prime minister, who repeatedly made ambiguous statements.
n2-set-14-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: aimai / あいまい - ambiguous, vague, equivocal.

choices.reason: For a dream that is indistinct, ぼんやりとした or かすかな fits, not あいまい.
あいまいな発言 correctly refers to vague or ambiguous political remarks.
If information is ambiguous (あいまい), it contradicts being likely true (確からしい); 不確かな would describe uncertainty.
For books left unread due to lack of time, 放置されている or 読まずじまい fits; あいまい cannot mean unfinished.

n2-set-14-q-31.translation: When explaining something to someone, speak while keeping to the main points.
n2-set-14-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: youten / 要点 - main point, gist, essential point.

choices.reason: For a speech summarized efficiently, 要領よく (skillfully/concisely) fits, not 要点よく.
For someone being clumsy or inept at tasks, 要領が悪い fits, not 要点が悪い.
要点をおさえて話す correctly uses 要点 for grasping and focusing on the core/essential points.
For famous sightseeing spots in an ancient capital, 名所 or 見どころ fits, not 要点.

n2-set-14-q-32.translation: The efficacy of this headache medicine lasts for about 12 hours.
n2-set-14-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: jizoku / 持続 - lasting, persisting, continuation (効き目が持続する = efficacy lasts).

choices.reason: 効き目が持続する is the natural and correct collocation for the effects of medicine persisting over time.
For driving continuously through the night without stopping, 連続して or 続けて fits, not 持続して.
For unpleasant incidents occurring repeatedly or in succession, 立て続けに or 連続して fits.
For food spoiling quickly or not keeping fresh, 日持ちしない (does not keep) fits, not 持続しない.

n2-set-14-q-33.translation: A: 'When was the exam again?' B: 'If I remember correctly, Yao said something like it's next week.'
n2-set-14-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: da to ka / だとか - something like ... / indirect hearsay of uncertain information.

choices.reason: だか does not naturally attach to quote reported information to a third party like this.
だとか expresses hearsay or indirect quotation where the speaker is not entirely certain of the exact detail.
だが is a conjunctive particle meaning 'but/however', not a hearsay marker.
だけど means 'however/although' and does not fit quoting Yao's statement.

n2-set-14-q-34.translation: As for my niece's cuteness, she is just like an angel!
n2-set-14-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: to ittara / といったら - speaking of ... / the extent of ... is extraordinary.

choices.reason: としたら sets up a hypothetical condition ('if we assume that...').
といえば brings up a topic based on association ('speaking of...').
といっても means 'even though one says...' (qualifying a statement).
といったら emphasizes the extreme degree of the niece's cuteness, matching まるで天使のようだ.

n2-set-14-q-35.translation: Precisely because I made the same mistake myself, I am warning you.
n2-set-14-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: kara koso / からこそ - precisely because, for the very reason that.

choices.reason: からこそ emphasizes the precise reason: it is exactly because the speaker failed that they are warning you.
からには means 'now that / since', expressing determination or obligation, not explaining the speaker's motive like this.
くせに expresses blame or contempt ('even though/despite'), which does not make sense here.
ことだから is used with people's character ('knowing him / since it is X'), not a personal past failure.

n2-set-14-q-36.translation: Our company publishes many books, focusing primarily on picture books for children.
n2-set-14-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: chuushin ni / 中心に - centered on, with a focus on.

choices.reason: 真ん中に refers to a physical middle spot, not an operational or thematic focus.
中心に (chuushin ni) means 'centered around / focusing primarily on', fitting the publisher's core lineup.
中央に refers to physical central location or central government.
最大に means 'at most' or 'to the maximum extent', which does not link a category to the rest of the publications.

n2-set-14-q-37.translation: The government instructed companies to recruit employees regardless of age.
n2-set-14-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: ni kakawarinaku / にかかわりなく - regardless of, irrespective of.

choices.reason: にかぎりなく means 'infinitely / boundlessly' (e.g. 限りなく透明), not regardless of.
にかかわりなく means 'regardless of / irrespective of', perfectly fitting recruitment open to all ages.
はぬきにして means 'leaving aside / omitting' (e.g. お世辞は抜きにして), which is not the legal/formal standard for recruitment.
のせいで means 'because of / due to (a bad cause)', which does not fit.

n2-set-14-q-38.translation: That person not only gave me directions, but even took the trouble of taking me all the way to the station.
n2-set-14-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: bakari ka / ばかりか - not only ... but even/also.

choices.reason: ばかりに expresses 'simply because of ... (an unfortunate result occurred)'.
ところに marks a temporal intersection ('just when...').
ばかりか expresses 'not only X, but also Y on top of it', matching the kind guide taking them to the station.
どころか means 'far from / on the contrary', contrasting an expectation with a reality, not additive kindness.

n2-set-14-q-39.translation: Taking the change of president as an opportunity / turning point, it was decided to change the company name.
n2-set-14-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: keiki ni shite / 契機にして - taking ... as an opportunity or turning point.

choices.reason: 事情にして is not an established grammatical pattern.
結果として means 'as a result', but does not take the を...として grammatical structure here.
を契機にして is the standard pattern meaning 'taking X as a trigger/turning point for a positive new step'.
原因にして is not a natural idiom; を原因として is occasionally used for causes of accidents, not institutional renewal.

n2-set-14-q-40.translation: You don't need to worry about the exam. With your level of academic ability, you are bound to pass.
n2-set-14-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: goukaku suru ni kimatte iru / 合格するに決まっている - bound to pass / certain to pass.

choices.reason: 合格するわけがある would imply there is a reason/justification, but わけがない is the normal pattern for impossibility; this phrasing is unnatural.
合格するものがある is ungrammatical; ものがある expresses a deep emotional quality ('there is something touching about...').
合格することに決めてある implies a personal plan decided beforehand, not an inevitable outcome.
合格するに決まっている expresses the speaker's firm conviction that passing is certain.

n2-set-14-q-41.translation: It is said that one should not give kitchen knives as wedding gifts, but if the recipient wants one, isn't it fine?
n2-set-14-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: okuru mono de wa nai / 贈るものではない - one should not give; it is improper to give.

choices.reason: 贈らないものでない is a double negative meaning 'it is not that one doesn't give', contrary to the Japanese cultural superstition against giving knives.
贈るものではない expresses a social norm or moral guideline: 'one ought not to give (knives as wedding gifts)'.
贈らないわけではない means 'it's not that I don't give', which does not express the customary prohibition.
贈るわけはない means 'there is no reason/way anyone would give', which does not fit the proverb-like advice.

n2-set-14-q-42.translation: People who do not push themselves too hard often end up lasting longer.
n2-set-14-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: ganbarisuginai / がんばりすぎない - not overdoing it / not pushing oneself too hard.

choices.reason: がんばるにすぎない means 'merely doing one's best', which does not fit modifying people who pace themselves.
がんばりすぎない means not pushing oneself beyond reasonable limits, which explains why they last longer (長続きする).
がんばろうとする means 'trying to do one's best', which would not explain the paradox marked by かえって (on the contrary).
がんばるばかりの means 'doing nothing but working hard', which would lead to burnout rather than lasting long.

n2-set-14-q-43.translation: Under normal circumstances the president himself should have come to visit you, but if you will excuse me, I, the department manager, have come instead.
n2-set-14-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: omimai ni kuru tokoro / お見舞いにくるところ - should properly be the situation where he comes to visit.

choices.reason: お見舞いにくるところ captures the nuance of 'the situation where he ought to come in person, but...'.
お見舞いされるはず means the president was supposed to be visited by others (passive), which reverses the courtesy.
お見舞いにくること merely nominalizes the action without the counterfactual contrast marked by 本来なら...ですが.
お見舞いにくるとき refers strictly to the time of arrival, which does not contrast properly with 本来なら.

n2-set-14-q-44.translation: A: 'It seems more people are acting violently at Coming-of-Age ceremonies.' B: 'In Japan, even upon turning 20, there are many people who are unable to fully become adults.'
n2-set-14-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: narikirenai / なりきれない - unable to become completely / fully mature.

choices.reason: なりそうもない means 'showing no signs of becoming / unlikely to become', which lacks the nuance of incomplete transition into adulthood.
なるはずがない means 'it is impossible that they become', which is too absolute and inaccurate.
なりきれない means unable to become fully or completely, perfectly describing young adults who remain immature.
なっていられない means 'cannot afford to stay as', which does not fit the grammar or context.

n2-set-14-q-45.translation: Pictographic marks are displayed so that even people who cannot read Japanese can understand them.
n2-set-14-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: you ni / ように - so that; option 2 sits at the star in 'にも 理解できる ように 絵による'.

choices.reason: にも attaches to 日本語が読めない人 to mean 'even for people who cannot read Japanese', placing it 1st.
ように follows the potential verb 理解できる to express purpose ('so that they can understand'), placing it 3rd at the star.
理解できる describes the ability of the non-readers, placing it 2nd after にも.
絵による modifies マーク ('marks based on pictures'), placing it 4th before マーク.

n2-set-14-q-46.translation: When you are hesitating over whether to do something or not, doing it often saves you from regret.
n2-set-14-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: ka to / かと - quoting hesitation between options; option 3 sits at the star in 'やめよう かと 迷ったときは やったほうが'.

choices.reason: やったほうが ('it is better to do it') serves as the subject phrase before 悔やまなくてすむ, placing it 4th.
迷ったときは ('when you are hesitating') sets the conditional context, placing it 3rd.
かと completes the quotation やろうかやめようかと ('wondering whether to do it or not'), placing it 2nd at the star.
やめよう balances やろうか to form the dilemma 'do it or refrain', placing it 1st.

n2-set-14-q-47.translation: A meeting was held to create new products based on customers' feedback.
n2-set-14-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: shite / して - based on (をもとにして); option 4 sits at the star in 'もとに して 新製品を 作る'.

choices.reason: 新製品を is the direct object of the verb 作る, placing it 3rd.
もとに follows お客様の意見を to start the pattern をもとにして, placing it 1st.
作る modifies ための会議 ('meeting for making...'), placing it 4th.
して completes the compound particle をもとにして ('based on'), placing it 2nd at the star.

n2-set-14-q-48.translation: After fiercely disputing over their parents' inheritance, the siblings ended up parting ways in bitter conflict.
n2-set-14-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: hageshiku arasotta / はげしく争った - fiercely disputed; option 4 sits at the star in 'めぐって 兄弟が はげしく争った あげく'.

choices.reason: めぐって follows 親の遺産を to mean 'concerning / over parents' inheritance', placing it 1st.
兄弟が is the grammatical subject performing the dispute, placing it 2nd.
あげく follows the past tense verb 争った to mean 'in the end after...', placing it 4th.
はげしく争った expresses the fierce fighting and sits 3rd at the star.

n2-set-14-q-49.translation: The reason why many housewives love traveling is not only that they enjoy seeing rare scenery, but also that they don't have to cook.
n2-set-14-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: ryouri o shinakute ii / 料理をしなくていい - not having to cook; option 1 sits at the star in '好きな だけでなく 料理をしなくていい ということ'.

choices.reason: 料理をしなくていい introduces the second benefit ('not having to cook'), placing it 3rd at the star.
好きな attaches to 見るのが to form 'liking to see...', placing it 1st.
だけでなく follows 好きな to mean 'not only liking...', placing it 2nd.
ということ nominalizes the clause before も理由の1つだ, placing it 4th.

n2-set-14-q-50.translation: Communication involves the process of taking information inward through 'listening' and 'reading', and transmitting information outward through 'speaking' and 'writing'.
n2-set-14-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: a yomu / b kaku - taking in input is reading (読む); transmitting output is writing (書く).

choices.reason: 'Reading' (読む) takes information in (中に取り入れる) alongside listening, while 'writing' (書く) transmits information outward (外に発信する) alongside speaking.
Reverses reading and writing, placing writing as input and reading as output.
Places speaking and listening into the blanks, which duplicates the words already in the sentence.
Places listening into b, which contradicts transmitting information outward.

n2-set-14-q-51.translation: Listening accounts for as much as 45% of time; nevertheless, practice in listening tends rarely to be conducted.
n2-set-14-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: ni mo kakawarazu / にもかかわらず - despite that / nevertheless.

choices.reason: だからこそ means 'precisely for that reason', which would illogically imply that high usage causes a lack of practice.
のために indicates purpose or negative causality, which does not link the contrasting facts.
それにもかかわらず ('in spite of that / nevertheless') correctly introduces the surprising contrast between 45% usage and the lack of listening training.
にしたがって means 'in accordance with / as X changes', which does not express contradiction.

n2-set-14-q-52.translation: This is likely because, whereas voices and sounds enter the ears naturally, speaking, reading, and writing are conscious activities.
n2-set-14-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: ishikiteki na / 意識的な - conscious, deliberate (contrasting with 自然に耳に入ってくる).

choices.reason: 無意識の means unconscious, which is the opposite of the active effort required for speaking, reading, and writing.
自然な means natural, failing to contrast with 'sounds entering the ear naturally' (自然に耳に入ってくる).
意識的な (conscious/deliberate) provides the exact contrast to sounds naturally entering the ears without effort.
不自然な means unnatural or awkward, which is not the distinction being made between passive sensation and active effort.

n2-set-14-q-53.translation: Next, listening to another person means paying attention to them, acknowledging their existence; conversely, if you do not listen, the person feels as if they have been rejected / denied.
n2-set-14-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: hitei sareta you ni / 否定されたように - as if they have been negated / rejected (the opposite of 存在を認める).

choices.reason: 攻撃されたように means as if attacked, which is an exaggerated physical/verbal assault rather than the denial of recognition.
否定されたように (as if rejected/denied) is the exact opposite of 存在を認める (acknowledging one's existence) marked by 逆に (conversely).
認められたように means as if recognized, which contradicts not listening to them.
注目されたように means as if paid attention to, which contradicts not listening.

n2-set-14-q-54.translation: By listening attentively to what they say, along with entering into a close relationship with the other person, they also come to feel goodwill toward you.
n2-set-14-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: naru to tomo ni / なるとともに - along with becoming ... / at the same time as becoming ...

choices.reason: なりそうになると means 'when it seems about to become', which introduces an uncertain prospective state.
なるとしても means 'even assuming that one enters', expressing a concession that contradicts the positive progression.
なるにつけても means 'whenever one enters', which does not fit linking two parallel outcomes.
なるとともに means 'along with becoming / at the same time as becoming', smoothly joining developing closeness and evoking goodwill.
